meta.title: A Biology Lesson at the Pond

paragraphs: A Biology Lesson at the Pond. By Lily, with photos by Mia. On Thursday, the Explorers had a biology lesson at the school pond. It was not a usual lesson, because we did not sit at desks. Teacher Kim planned it, and she gave every group a job. We stood on the grass around the pond, and Teacher Kim asked us to keep quiet. This post tells you what we did and what we found. Use the headings to find the facts.

The Plan on the Blackboard. Before the lesson, Teacher Kim wrote the plan on the blackboard in our classroom. There were three steps: look, catch, and write. Teacher Kim also drew a small frog next to the plan. First, we look at the water for five minutes. Then we catch small animals with a net. Finally, we write their names in a table.

The Equipment. Each group had one net, two white boxes, and a magnifying glass. We also had a pencil and a paper table. Leo carried the boxes, and May carried the nets to the pond. It rained in the morning. Luckily, the rain stopped one hour before the lesson. At the end, Teacher Kim asked us to wash our hands.

What We Found. We found twelve tadpoles, three snails, and one water beetle. A tadpole is a baby frog, and it has a long tail. The beetle was black, and it swam very fast. The snails moved slowly on a green leaf. Mia put the beetle in a white box and took a photo. Leo counted the animals, and I wrote the names in our table. Photo by Mia: the water beetle in a white box.

A Funny Moment. Leo performed a short comedy for his group. He used a green sock as a frog. The frog said, "Please do not catch me!" in a very small voice. Everybody laughed, and even Teacher Kim smiled. May laughed so much that she nearly dropped her net. It was the best part of the day for the whole group.

Our Success. At the end, every group had a full table of names. We put all the animals back into the pond. Teacher Kim says, "The lesson was a success." A tadpole grows legs and becomes a frog after some weeks. A snail has a hard shell, and it carries its home on its back. Which fact do you like best? Tell us in a message!
